crossing supervisor Listen Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Print Content components School crossing supervisors have a much-valued role in Boroondara. On an average school day in Boroondara, they help 9,266 pedestrians to cross the street while 74,426 motor vehicles use our roads during school crossing times. We are always looking for school crossing supervisors. If you are friendly, reliable and flexible, this role is for you. What does a school crossing supervisor do? This paid position gives you the opportunity to get involved in your community and improve road safety for children, people with a disability and the general public who use our 114 school crossings. School crossing supervisors: • work part-time Monday to Friday, from 8 am to 9 am and from 3 pm to 4 pm, during the school term • play an important role in educating children with ‘Stop, Look and Listen’ instructions • are responsible for reporting any road hazards or potential risks • help to encourage active and independent travel. About you We are looking for people aged 18 and older who: • can attend shifts at short notice • have their own reliable transport • are able to work across several locations • can complete the pre-employment medical and police checks. You will have access to a full training program before starting your role. Submit an online application through our Careers website . Attend an interview – meet with one of our Council Officers at Council, located at 8 Inglesby Road in Camberwell. Provide us with relevant employment documents – including your Working With Children Check, Police Check and evidence of your COVID-19 vaccination status. Complete a medical assessment. Apply to become a School Crossings Supervisor We are always recruiting new school crossing supervisors to help people to cross our roads safely at peak school times. A little bit about the role You will work closely with our families to provide advice, support, and guidance through the critical foundational years for each family. The role will be responsible for, but not limited to: Promoting healthy outcomes for children and their families. Providing a comprehensive and focused approach to managing the physical, emotional, or social factors affecting families in contemporary communities. Providing opportunities for social interaction of the parent and child. Providing families with timely, accurate and relevant information and resources to assist them achieve and maintain maximum health potential. Skills and experience to thrive in the role Demonstrated clinical experience in Maternal & Child Health. Commitment to family centred practice within an integrated early years’ service mode. Awareness of child and family health issues, normal child development, family dynamics and promotion of maternal wellbeing. Familiarity with MCH & immunisation programs across Boroondara. Demonstrated awareness of smalltalk, Parent Child Mother Goose and Circle of Security programs. Experience in sleep and settling program delivery, including day stay and outreach services desirable Able to use computer systems, including Microsoft Word, Microsoft Outlook, icope and CDIS. Qualifications & employment requirements Registered General Division 1 Nurse & Midwife with AHPRA registration A post graduate qualification in Maternal & Child Health Nursing IBCLC qualification Immunisation qualification preferred Ability to work independently, and within a multidisciplinary team Commitment to family centred practice within an integrated early years’ service model Demonstrated clinical experience in Maternal & Child Health Aware of child and family health issues, normal child development, family dynamics & promotion of maternal well being High levels of written and oral communication skills Conversant with relevant health promotion issues How to Apply Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by 11:59pm Thursday 29 October 2026. If you want to know more about the benefits of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our Careers Website. Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Relief Librarian (15266) Requisition ID 15266 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Relief Librarian Relief role working across all library sites (weekdays and weekends) $44.08 per hour Band 5 plus 25% loading Are you passionate about connecting people with information, ideas and community? We're seeking enthusiastic and customer-focused Relief Librarians to join our Library Services team on a casual basis and support our vibrant network of libraries across Boroondara. In this varied role, you'll provide high-quality customer service, professional readers' advisory and information services, and support the day-to-day operations of our libraries. You'll have the opportunity to work across multiple library locations, helping community members access our collections, digital resources, programs and services. What you'll do Deliver exceptional frontline customer service in person, by phone and online. Provide readers' advisory, reference and information services. Promote library collections, digital resources, programs and events. Support library operations, including opening and closing procedures, cash handling and maintaining welcoming library spaces. Assist with collection presentation, stock management and merchandising. Supervise service delivery and support staff when rostered as Day Senior. Work collaboratively across library locations to meet service needs. About you You are a customer-focused library professional who enjoys working with diverse communities and thrives in a flexible, fast-paced environment. You will bring: A tertiary qualification that confers eligibility for professional membership of the Australian Library and Information Association (ALIA). Experience working in a library environment, preferably within a public library. Strong customer service and communication skills. The ability to confidently assist customers with digital technology and information tools. Demonstrated ability to supervise, support and mentor staff. Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Office and web-based technologies. An appreciation of diverse cultures and communities; additional language skills are highly regarded. Why join us? At City of Boroondara, we're committed to creating a healthy, connected and sustainable community. Our people are guided by our values of Innovate, Integrity, Respect, Own-it, Collaborate and Customer, and we work together to deliver outstanding services that make a difference every day. What's on offer? Flexible work across multiple library locations. Opportunities for evening, weekend and school holiday shifts. A supportive team environment serving one of Melbourne's most engaged library communities. More information Read the position description or call Kate Finn, Branch Lead Hawthorn on 7074 2109 during business hours. How to Apply Apply online by 11:59pm Tuesday 27 October 2026 . Applications sent directly to the hiring manager will not be considered. If you want to know more about the benefits of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our Careers Website. Council recognises the benefits of a diverse workforce for its employees and customers. To ensure equity of access to employment opportunities, Council encourages applications from underrepresented groups including people who are from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander background, people from different ages, abilities, gender identities, sexual orientation and cultural backgrounds. If you require any additional support or adjustments regarding interview arrangements, please advise the contact listed above in advance. Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Council is a child safe organisation and as such, some applicants may be required to hold a Working with Children Clearance. Additionally, some applicants may also be required to undergo a National Criminal History check and/or medical check as per the requirements of the role. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. You will be instrumental in driving this change across the organisation using best practice approaches to successfully support us from the now to our desired future state. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Library Officer (Customer Support) (15269) Requisition ID 15269 - Posted - Job Function (3) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Library Officer (Customer Support) Part-time temporary position until 22 August 2027 (14hrs per week spread over Tuesday, Wednesday & Friday) Fantastic opportunity to join our dynamic Library Services team! $78,621 - $84,734 Band 4 (pro rata to be applied) plus Superannuation This position is primarily based at the Greythorn Library Lounge but is expected to work across all library location as needed If you enjoy working with people, thrive in a busy customer service environment and have outstanding interpersonal skills,, this may be the perfect opportunity for you. Join our dynamic library service and play a key role in creating positive experiences for our community. Please note that all positions require regular evening and weekend work. A little bit about the role The Library Officer (Customer Support) plays an important role in delivering outstanding customer experiences across our library service. Working collaboratively with the Customer Support team and broader library staff, this position supports the day-to-day delivery of library services by assisting customers with enquiries, managing circulation and membership transactions, and promoting library collections, programs and events. Through friendly, responsive and professional service, the Library Officer helps create a welcoming and engaging environment for all library users. What will you bring to the role? We are seeking a motivated and customer-focused individual to join our team and help deliver exceptional library experiences for the Boroondara community. You will be passionate about providing outstanding customer service, enjoy working with a diverse range of people, and thrive in a collaborative environment. To be successful in this role you will have: Well-developed interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with people from diverse backgrounds. Experience in a frontline customer service role; experience in a public library environment will be highly regarded. Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to adapt, learn and respond to changing situations. Effective time management and organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise work and respond to customer demand. A positive, proactive approach and a commitment to delivering high-quality customer experiences. The successful applicant will also have: A relevant post-secondary qualification Confidence using a variety of digital devices and consumer technologies. Strong computer skills, including experience with Microsoft Office applications and online systems. The ability to lift, push or carry library resources around library facilities (subject to appropriate Occupational Health and Safety regulations), and A current driver's license (advantageous). Employment Requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check and hold a valid Working with Children Clearance. Subject to a satisfactory medical check How to Apply Please submit your application online via the ‘ Apply’ button by 23 October 2026 . All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager will be considered. No calls or applications from agencies please. We encourage you to submit your application early, if there is sufficient response, the advertisement period may close earlier than 23 October, 2026 For any further information please refer to the position description , or contact Gitte Mortensen during business hours on 9278 4339 for a confidential discussion. If you want to know more about the benefits of working for the City of Boroondara, please visit our Careers Website. Council recognises the benefits of a diverse workforce for its employees and customers. To ensure equity of access to employment opportunities, Council encourages applications from underrepresented groups including people who are from an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander background, people from different ages, abilities, gender identities, sexual orientation and cultural backgrounds. If you require any additional support or adjustments regarding interview arrangements, please advise the contact listed above in advance. Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Council is a child safe organisation and as such, some applicants may be required to hold a Working with Children Clearance. Additionally, some applicants may also be required to undergo a National Criminal History check and/or medical check as per the requirements of the role. Working together We are currently undertaking an exciting project that will see a transformation in the way we work and the way we serve our customers. Implementation of the Boroondara Customer First Program will provide a customer centric model of service delivery that includes technological innovation, process improvement and business system renewal - we value your input and look forward to our journey ahead. Skip to Main Content Career Opportunities: Business and Policy Analyst (15275) Requisition ID 15275 - Posted - Job Function (1) - Tenure Status (1) - Employment Status (1)  Job Description Print Preview Apply Save Job Email Job to Friend Return to List Do you love data like we do? A unique role focused on technology, innovation and with high exposure! $87,101 - $100,905 per annum plus Super and RDO leave 4:1 hybrid working offered This is a specialised role offering diverse responsibilities and exposure across the organisation, with close connection to senior leadership. The role provides an opportunity to build experience across technology, data analytics, project management, business improvement and corporate functions. A little bit about the role The Business and Policy Analyst will play a key role in supporting parking technology, innovation and continuous improvement, including analysing data, monitoring performance and providing insights to inform operational strategy and service improvements. A parking technology roadmap is being progressed, and this role will be a key contributor delivering it alongside the Business and Policy Lead and Manager Civic Services. The role also includes ongoing administrative responsibilities, including producing insightful reporting and metrics, supporting contract management and vendor meetings, procurement and invoice management, and maintaining strong business records. Exciting projects and business improvement opportunities will also be assigned as capacity permits. This provides variety and ensures the role continues to evolve and grow. Reporting to the Business and Policy Lead, key aspects of the role include: Leading innovation across parking technology, including market research, consultation and refining approaches with Parking Services leadership. Analysing large datasets and producing insights on parking operations to inform strategic approaches and future service models. Providing data and recommendations that inform strategic decisions and have a tangible impact on the regulatory services delivered to the community. Supporting leadership with parking contract management, enhancement and maintenance. Providing direct support to the Business and Policy Lead through the coordination and delivery of delegated priorities as they arise. Providing first-class customer service to internal and external stakeholders in a professional and courteous manner. Providing project management support for key departmental projects and continuous improvement initiatives. Managing invoicing, including raising purchase orders, receipting goods and maintaining accurate financial records for the Coordinator. Providing advocacy and quality assurance across Civic Services on key legislative and auditing functions. A little bit about you Your skills are the foundation of our success. The skills and experience you bring: A love of data, getting into the detail, and pulling out the insights to tell the real story of what’s occurring. Expertise in project management, continuous improvement and delivering outcomes to support front-line teams that are servicing the community. A fun and energetic approach to work that’s outgoing and engaging. Natural ability to manage personal time, to set priorities and plan and organise own work to efficiently complete tasks or achieve objectives within agreed time frames. Excellent records management and Microsoft Office skills experience, particularly in Excel and PowerPoint. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including demonstrated ability in writing accurate and comprehensive reports and correspondence. A sound knowledge or ability to gain the knowledge of relevant Regulations and Council policies. Relevant experience in a complex customer service/administrative environment both in person and over the phone, including proficiency in financial administration, preferably in local government or other statutory based environments. Want to know more? For further information about this opportunity please refer to the Position Description or contact Yvonne Hill , Business and Policy Lead during business hours on 9248 4444 for a confidential discussion. What sets us apart? A supportive and friendly workplace culture that values diversity, collaboration and continuous improvement. Staff benefits such as flexible working arrangements, wellbeing programs, gym and pool memberships An investment in your ongoing professional development and career growth Employment requirements Applicants must have the right to work in Australia. Preferred applicants will be required to undergo a National Police Record Check and hold a valid Working With Children’s check. How to apply (follow carefully) Please submit your application online via the ‘Apply’ button by Tuesday 20 October 2026, 11:59pm . All applications must be made via the online portal; no applications direct to the hiring manager or from recruitment agencies will be considered. We understand that this portal may not meet the needs of people who rely on Assistive Technology or have other diverse requirements. If you have any difficulty using our recruitment system, please do not hesitate to contact People Culture and Development on (03) 9278 4401 or pcd@boroondara.vic.gov.au to allow us to help in any way we can. Who are we? The City of Boroondara is a metropolitan council, representing more than 170,000 people in the inner-eastern suburbs of Melbourne. A leader in the local government sector, with a reputation for innovation and excellence, we believe in providing an environment where our staff thrive, both in the work they do and in how they learn and develop as people and professionals. We like to challenge the norm and we are investing significantly in innovation and technology improvements in order to provide our customers with an even greater experience and engagement. We are putting our customers at the forefront of what we do with our organisation wide initiative, Transforming Boroondara Program. We are seeking skilled and experienced professional care workers who love supporting people to live independently in the community. We currently provide services in Mount Alexander Shire and Central Goldfields Shire. This is your opportunity to bring your passion and skills to be part of a professional and dedicated team providing high quality in-home support to frail older people and people with disabilities in our community. The role provides tailored services to help clients live healthy, independent and active lives through assistance with daily tasks and activities. Direct Care Worker Traineeship Opportunities: If you don’t already have a certificate III in Individual Support, you can also apply here for a Trainee Direct Care Worker position, to earn and learn on the job. Minimum Qualifications and Experience You must have, or be willing to obtain: Current Police Check Current Working with Children Check Triple vaccinated for COVID (2 doses plus a booster). Current Drivers license and roadworthy, registered and comprehensively insured vehicle for work travel Applicants must be able to work weekends. First Aid and CPR certificate will be gained though training and applied to the role as required If you have any queries or would like to discuss the role, the key contacts are: Sarah Newstead In Home Support Coordinator – East (03) 5471 1845 Talia Jenkin In Home Support Coordinator – West (03) 5471 1728 To apply for a Direct Care Worker or Direct Care Worker Trainee position, please provide a cover letter (no more than 2 pages) outlining why you are interested and the best candidate for this role, and your current resume. Additional information Mount Alexander Shire Council is committed to providing a safe, inclusive, and respectful workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer and are committed to child safety with zero tolerance for child abuse. We value a diverse workforce and encourage applicants from all cultures, sexual orientations, gender identities and backgrounds. Applicants can expect that the recruitment process will include interviewing, reference checks and criminal history checks. Some positions will also be required to provide a Working with Children Check, and medical assessments including drug and alcohol testing may be undertaken. For more information on the recruitment process, please download the Candidate information document from our website. Join us to improve the health, development, learning and well-being of children, their mothers, and families from pregnancy through transition to school. Our Maternal and Child Health Program The Maternal and Child Health service (MCH) is free and provides primary care to postnatal women and children from birth to school age. The service supports families with an emphasis on parenting education, social support groups, health promotion and prevention, developmental assessment, and early intervention. Maternal and child health nurses are registered nurses and midwives who have tertiary qualifications in child and family health nursing. Some nurses also have additional qualifications in perinatal and infant mental health, immunisation and lactation consultant accreditation. The MCH team aims to give our community the very best support and the latest evidence-based information to promote child health and development, and to support parent’s wellbeing. Enhanced Maternal and Child Health Services The Enhanced Maternal and Child Health Service is a home visiting program provided by Maternal and Child Health Nurses and Social Workers to assist families by providing extra support and guidance. It is in addition to the suite of services offered through the Universal MCH service. It provides a more intensive level of support and responds assertively to the needs of children and families who may be at risk. Telephone referrals are accepted from GPs, child and family services or allied health professionals.
